# Normal distribution

import numpy as np
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
from scipy import stats

print("=== The Normal Distribution ===\n")

print("The normal distribution is the most important distribution in statistics.")
print("""
Characteristics:
  ✅ Bell-shaped
  ✅ Symmetric around mean
  ✅ Mean = Median = Mode
  ✅ 68-95-99.7 rule
""")

print("=== 68-95-99.7 Rule ===\n")

# Create normal distribution
mu = 50  # mean
sigma = 10  # standard deviation
x = np.linspace(mu - 4*sigma, mu + 4*sigma, 1000)
y = stats.norm.pdf(x, mu, sigma)

plt.figure(figsize=(12, 6))
plt.plot(x, y, 'b-', linewidth=2, label='Normal Distribution')

# Shade regions
# ±1 sigma (68%)
plt.axvspan(mu - sigma, mu + sigma, alpha=0.2, color='blue', label='68%')
# ±2 sigma (95%)
plt.axvspan(mu - 2*sigma, mu - sigma, alpha=0.1, color='green', label='95%')
plt.axvspan(mu + sigma, mu + 2*sigma, alpha=0.1, color='green')
# ±3 sigma (99.7%)
plt.axvspan(mu - 3*sigma, mu - 2*sigma, alpha=0.05, color='red', label='99.7%')
plt.axvspan(mu + 2*sigma, mu + 3*sigma, alpha=0.05, color='red')

plt.axvline(mu, color='black', linestyle='--', alpha=0.5)
plt.xlabel('Value')
plt.ylabel('Probability Density')
plt.title('Normal Distribution: 68-95-99.7 Rule')
plt.legend()
plt.grid(True, alpha=0.3)
plt.show()

print("\n=== Generating Normal Data ===\n")

# Generate data
np.random.seed(42)
data = np.random.normal(mu, sigma, 10000)

print(f"Mean: {np.mean(data):.2f}")
print(f"Std Dev: {np.std(data):.2f}")

# Calculate percentages in each range
print("\nEmpirical percentages:")
print(f"Within 1 sigma: {sum((data > mu - sigma) & (data < mu + sigma)) / len(data) * 100:.1f}%")
print(f"Within 2 sigma: {sum((data > mu - 2*sigma) & (data < mu + 2*sigma)) / len(data) * 100:.1f}%")
print(f"Within 3 sigma: {sum((data > mu - 3*sigma) & (data < mu + 3*sigma)) / len(data) * 100:.1f}%")

print("\n=== Standard Normal Distribution (Z-score) ===\n")

# Z-score: (x - mu) / sigma
z_scores = (data - mu) / sigma
print(f"Z-score mean: {np.mean(z_scores):.2f}")
print(f"Z-score std dev: {np.std(z_scores):.2f}")

# Z-score table
print("\nZ-score table (standard normal):")
for z in [-3, -2, -1, 0, 1, 2, 3]:
    prob = stats.norm.cdf(z)
    print(f"  Z={z}: P(X <= {z}) = {prob:.4f}")

print("\n=== Visualizing Different Normals ===\n")

# Different means and standard deviations
means = [0, 0, 0, 5]
stds = [1, 2, 3, 1]
labels = ['μ=0, σ=1', 'μ=0, σ=2', 'μ=0, σ=3', 'μ=5, σ=1']

plt.figure(figsize=(10, 6))

x = np.linspace(-10, 10, 1000)
for mu_i, sigma_i, label in zip(means, stds, labels):
    y = stats.norm.pdf(x, mu_i, sigma_i)
    plt.plot(x, y, label=label, linewidth=2)

plt.title('Different Normal Distributions')
plt.xlabel('Value')
plt.ylabel('Probability Density')
plt.legend()
plt.grid(True, alpha=0.3)
plt.show()

print("\n=== When to use normal distribution ===\n")

print("Use normal distribution when:")
print("  ✅ Data is symmetric")
print("  ✅ Data is unimodal")
print("  ✅ Data follows the 68-95-99.7 rule")
print("  ✅ Inferential statistics (t-tests, ANOVA, regression)")

phase1.explanation:
🐍 **The normal distribution is the foundation of statistics.**

**Properties:**
- Bell-shaped and symmetric
- Mean = Median = Mode
- 68-95-99.7 rule

**68-95-99.7 Rule:**
- 68% within ±1 standard deviation
- 95% within ±2 standard deviations
- 99.7% within ±3 standard deviations

**Z-score:**
```python

stats.norm.ppf(p)  # z for probability p
```

# Assuming normal distribution without checking

import numpy as np
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

# Create non-normal data
data = np.random.exponential(1, 1000)

# Calculate statistics
mean = np.mean(data)
std = np.std(data)

print(f"Mean: {mean:.2f}")
print(f"Std Dev: {std:.2f}")
print(f"Skewness: {stats.skew(data):.2f}")

# If we assumed normal, we'd make wrong conclusions
# Always check the distribution first!

# Visual check
plt.figure(figsize=(10, 4))
plt.subplot(1, 2, 1)
plt.hist(data, bins=30)
plt.title('Data Distribution')
plt.subplot(1, 2, 2)
stats.probplot(data, dist='norm', plot=plt)
plt.title('Q-Q Plot')
plt.show()

print("\nQ-Q plot shows deviation from normal (points don't follow line)")

phase2.explanation:
**Don't assume normality without checking!**

**What's wrong:**
1. Data is exponential (skewed)
2. Not normal
3. Using normal-based methods would be wrong

**The fix:**
```python
import numpy as np
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
from scipy import stats

# Method 1: Visual check - histogram
plt.hist(data, bins=30)
plt.title('Check distribution')
plt.show()

# Method 2: Q-Q plot
stats.probplot(data, dist='norm', plot=plt)
plt.title('Q-Q Plot (should be straight line)')
plt.show()

# Method 3: Shapiro-Wilk test
stat, p = stats.shapiro(data)
print(f"Shapiro-Wilk test: stat={stat:.3f}, p={p:.3f}")
if p > 0.05:
    print("Data appears normal (fail to reject H0)")
else:
    print("Data is not normal (reject H0)")

# Method 4: Use non-parametric methods if not normal
# - Median instead of mean
# - Mann-Whitney instead of t-test
# - Spearman instead of Pearson
```

**Python-chan says:**
"Always check normality before using normal-based methods."
